title: Work Item
description: One compiled Work Item: an Objective's sub-issue (§3.1), described fully enough to become both a GitHub issue and an Agent Tasks prompt (§8's Work Packet -> prompt) with no further judgment required at dispatch time.

id.description: Compiler-local identifier, unique within one compiled graph. It is stored only inside Factory's immutable graph record and per-item graph envelope, and is used to express `dependsOn` edges before corresponding issue numbers exist.

title.description: GitHub issue title, used verbatim for the sub-issue.

goal.description: One sentence: what this Work Item accomplishes (§8).

acceptance.description: Explicit, checkable criteria (§8). Each entry must be verifiable from the diff alone: the semantic check (§5.2) tests these against the pull request, never against the agent's self-report (§11.7).

scope.description: Files or directories (trailing '/' scopes a whole directory) this Work Item may modify (§8). A one-line scope constraint holds reliably in practice (docs/PLATFORM-BEHAVIOR.md). This is also `evaluate.ts`'s `isUntouched` input -- keep entries concrete paths, not glob patterns.

preconditions.description: What must already be true for this Work Item to be actionable (§8). A well-specified precondition is what lets the agent decline rather than invent (§5.3) -- e.g. 'the file being modified already exists'.

outOfScope.description: Explicit non-goals (§8) -- guards against the agent silently widening scope beyond `scope`.

conventions.description: Repo-specific constraints the agent must follow (§8) -- test/build commands, commit style, file layout conventions.

dependsOn.description: IDs (this schema's `id` field, not issue numbers) of Work Items that must finish first. `graph.ts` applies them as native GitHub 'blocked by' relationships. Every entry must resolve, the graph must be acyclic, and any pair with overlapping scope must have a dependency path; runtime graph validation enforces these cross-item invariants before the first issue write.

baseSha.description: Exact repository commit observed during compilation. The Supervisor refreshes the execution copy to the current default-branch SHA only after dependencies clear, and records that actual SHA in the attempt reservation.

validationCommands.description: Authoritative host-side commands that must pass in a fresh checkout before publication.
